title: Night of the Dead: A Radio Play
teaser: During the live broadcast of the radio play Night of the Dead, the narrator screamed, and the listeners thought it was part of the show. Howard Lang lies by the microphone, and in his script the last line has been struck out in ink, with someone else's hand writing over it: "The narrator falls silent for ever." The broadcast ran to the end because nobody dared stop it, and now everyone in the studio insists they were in their place.

habits.label: Coconut shells
habits.habit: Carries coconut halves in their pocket for hoofbeats
clues: The floor of the announcers' dressing room has fibrous crumbs of coconut shell, and coconuts are brought to the station only for hoofbeats. The culprit has coconut shells in their pocket.
On the roof by the antenna a split coconut half, the kind used to knock out hoofbeats on air, was dropped by the parapet. The culprit carries coconut shells.

habits.label: Scrunches cellophane
habits.habit: Scrunches cellophane in their fingers when nervous
clues: In the live studio there's a crumpled ball of cellophane under Lang's music stand, and the fire in the play crackles in another corner. The culprit scrunches cellophane when nervous.
In the record library a tight wad of crumpled cellophane rustles between the record sleeves. The culprit has a habit of scrunching cellophane.

habits.label: Skeleton tie
habits.habit: A black tie embroidered with a white skeleton
clues: A magazine photographer was snapping guests in the station director's office, and at the edge of one frame there's a tie with a white skeleton, but the face is out of shot. The culprit has a skeleton tie.
In the record library a white silk embroidery thread on a scrap of black silk hangs on a shelf nail. The culprit wears a black tie embroidered with a skeleton.

habits.label: Orange paint
habits.habit: Fingers stained with orange paint from the paper pumpkins
clues: The black handle of the live studio door has an orange fingerprint, the paint still sticky. The culprit has orange paint on their fingers.
The rung of the hatch to the roof has orange smears of the same paint as the paper pumpkins in the studio. The culprit has pumpkin-orange paint on their fingers.

habits.label: Dead man's mask
habits.habit: A cardboard dead man's mask hanging round their neck
clues: In the sound effects room a snapped elastic from a cardboard mask dangles on a nail, with white cardboard crumbs beside it. The culprit wears a cardboard dead man's mask round their neck.
The switchboard girl saw a white cardboard face with black holes for eyes behind the glass door of the announcers' dressing room. The culprit has a dead man's mask.

habits.label: Skull badge
habits.habit: The play's tin skull badge on their lapel
clues: A tin skull badge with a bent pin is stuck between the records in the record library. The culprit wears a skull badge.
The lift boy saw a little tin skull flash on a lapel on the stairs to the control room. The culprit has a skull badge on their lapel.

habits.label: Stopwatch round the neck
habits.habit: Always has a stopwatch on a cord round their neck
clues: In the control room a torn cord with a brass ring, the kind a stopwatch hangs from, dangles on the hook by the door. The culprit wears a stopwatch round their neck.
The cleaner in the announcers' dressing room heard loud ticking behind the screen and the click of a stopwatch being started. The culprit has a stopwatch on a cord.

habits.label: Pencil behind the ear
habits.habit: Always has a red pencil behind their ear
clues: In the station director's office the penalty clause in Lang's contract is underlined in red pencil. The culprit keeps a red pencil behind their ear.
On the roof under a mast stay lies a red pencil sharpened with a penknife. The culprit has a red pencil behind their ear.

habits.label: Deep bass voice
habits.habit: A deep bass voice you can hear through two walls
clues: On the broadcast's reference disc in the control room, a second before the scream a deep bass voice off-script tells Lang "Quiet." The culprit has a deep bass voice.
A singer from the choir heard a voice from the sound effects room so deep that the glass in the door rattled. The culprit speaks in a deep bass.

habits.label: Cherry tobacco
habits.habit: Smokes a pipe of cherry tobacco
clues: In the announcers' dressing room, where smoking is banned for the sake of voices, there's sweet cherry smoke. The culprit smells of cherry tobacco.
On the roof by a ventilation pipe someone knocked out a pipe: a little heap of ash with a cherry smell. The culprit smokes a pipe of cherry tobacco.

habits.label: Violet ink
habits.habit: Middle finger stained with violet ink
clues: The writing over Lang's line in the live studio is in violet ink, and there's a smudged fingerprint of the same colour in the margin. The culprit has a finger stained with violet ink.
In the station director's office the blotter has fresh violet fingerprints, though only black ink stands on the desk. The culprit's middle finger is stained with violet ink.

habits.label: Lavender cologne
clues: The record library, which smells only of dust and shellac, holds a smell of lavender. The culprit smells of lavender cologne.
Lang's script in the live studio smells of lavender, though Lang wore only sandalwood. The culprit smells of lavender.

habits.label: Plaster on a finger
habits.habit: A finger wrapped in a strip of sticking plaster
clues: In the sound effects room a plaster that came unstuck hangs on the sharp edge of the thunder sheet. The culprit has a finger wrapped in plaster.
In the control room there's a sticky square from a plaster on the volume knob. The culprit has a plaster on their finger.

habits.label: Two-tone shoes
clues: The fireman on duty remembered only feet in white-and-brown shoes walking from the station director's office to the stairs. The culprit wears two-tone shoes.
In the sound effects room, by the sandbox used for footsteps, someone left a jar of whitener for cleaning pale shoe leather. The culprit wears two-tone shoes, white and brown.

habits.label: Hums the soap jingle
habits.habit: Hums a verse from the soap advert
clues: A violinist from the orchestra heard someone in the empty record library humming the soap advert jingle under their breath. The culprit hums the soap advert.
In the announcers' dressing room two lines of the soap jingle are written on the mirror with a sliver of soap. The culprit is always humming the soap advert.

habits.label: Rabbit's foot
habits.habit: A lucky rabbit's foot on a chain
clues: Under the desk in the control room there's a tuft of grey rabbit fur with a ring from a chain. The culprit has a rabbit's foot on a chain.
A grey rabbit's foot lies by the microphone stand in the live studio, and Lang didn't believe in omens and mocked lucky charms. The culprit carries a lucky rabbit's foot.

sched: It all happened during the organ interlude, when by the script only Lang stands at the microphone in the live studio. The culprit knows the schedule.
At 22:45 the floor patrol goes off on schedule towards the stairs to the roof, and the corridor by the studio is empty for two minutes. The culprit knows the schedule.
passages: A low props door leads from the sound effects room to the live studio. Only insiders know about it, and its bolt is drawn back. The culprit knows the service passages.
In the record library, behind a shelf of records, there's a door to the back stairs, and the shelf has been pulled out a hand's width. The culprit knows the service passages.
tech: The red "On Air" lamp over the live studio door went out for half a minute: its wire was pulled from the terminal and put back. The culprit knows their way around machinery.

In the control room the volume of Lang's microphone was turned almost to zero just before the scream, then the knob was returned to its mark, so the scream sounded muffled on air, as if from far away. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
tools: A guy wire of the antenna on the roof was loosened two turns with a spanner, and the interference on air began at exactly the right minute. The culprit is handy with tools.
The props box in the sound effects room was opened with a screwdriver: the lock plate was taken off and screwed back on, every screw in place. The culprit is handy with tools.
strong: The thunder sheet in the sound effects room was taken off its hooks and leaned against the wall, and it takes two to lift. The culprit is physically strong.
The hatch to the roof is weighed down against the wind with a cast-iron slab, yet it was flung open with a single heave. The culprit is physically strong.
quiet: In the live studio the microphone catches every rustle, yet the reference disc has not a single footstep until the scream. The culprit moves silently.
The parquet in the record library creaks by every shelf, yet in the announcers' dressing room next door nobody heard anything during the whole broadcast. The culprit moves silently.
medic: The glass of water by Lang's microphone has a bitterish taste, and the carafe in the announcers' dressing room has been washed, though it isn't washed until morning. The culprit knows about poisons.
A bottle of foxglove heart drops is missing from the first-aid kit in the station director's office, and in a large dose such drops stop the heart. The culprit knows about poisons.
french: Under the stranger's writing in Lang's script in the live studio, someone has added in small letters "C'est la fin du conte", French for "The tale is over". The culprit knows French.
In the record library the first line on the sleeve of a Paris chanson record has been translated in pencil, and translated correctly. The culprit knows French.
cash: The envelope with Lang's fee in the station director's office is empty, and the cash book already marks it as paid in someone else's hand. The culprit had access to money.

In the bin by the control room there's a bank band from the bundle brought in during the day for the broadcast participants' fees, and the bundle itself isn't in the safe. The culprit had access to money.
safe: The safe in the station director's office was opened with the combination, and Lang's contract is missing from it. The culprit knows the safe combination.

The fireproof cabinet in the record library where recordings of past broadcasts are kept was opened without a pick, and last week's disc of Lang's voice is missing. The culprit knows the safe combination.
keys: The door to the roof is padlocked, yet tonight the padlock was taken off with a key and hung back open. The culprit had keys.
The announcers' dressing room is locked during broadcasts, yet it was unlocked, with not a scratch on the lock. The culprit had keys.
